newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Deng placed briefly in intensive care - paper.
newsitem.headline: China's Deng placed briefly in intensive care - paper.

text.p: China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping was placed in intensive care after he fell unconscious briefly on Monday night, Hong Kong's South China Morning Post reported.

Nurses tending Deng, the 92-year-old patriarch and architect of China's sweeping economic reforms, were unable to wake him for supper and placed him in intensive care in his ward-like house in Beijing after he recovered consciousness later that night, the newspaper said on Wednesday.
The report could not be independently confirmed in Beijing.
Deng had experienced a "spell of unconsciousness" about once a week since early last year, the paper quoted a source close to the family as saying on Tuesday.
But the source denied newspaper reports that Deng had recently been admitted to hospital.

The independent Sing Tao Daily published in Hong Kong quoted an informed Beijing source as saying Deng's health had recently deteriorated and was sent to a military hospital in Beijing's western suburbs last week.
Deng's health had deteriorated in much the same way as other patients suffering from the advanced stage of Parkinson's disease, the Morning Post quoted the source as saying.

The independent Ming Pao Daily also quoted on Wednesday a spokesman of Xinhua News Agency's Hong Kong branch as saying reports that Deng was admitted to the hospital in a critical state were unfounded.
China's Central television station is scheduled to launch a 12-part documentary on Deng's life and times, lauding the leader's achievements.
The Morning Post quoted a party source in Beijing as saying there was no direct connection between Deng's health and the documentary.
President Jiang Zemin and the Deng household began preparing for the series more than a year ago, the source said.
